chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: Going to Long Branch, New Jersey with Tommy Chase, 1941
summary: In June 1941 Phillips joined a six-piece summer band led by pianist-trumpeter Tommy Chase, with tenor Leo Williams; Dupre and Phillips mix up Leo Williams and Leo Parker.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Back to 1941. You left Tommy Miles, and then you said you went up to New Jersey.
Long Branch, New Jersey.
What month was that again?
In June.
In June 1941 you went to Long Branch, New Jersey. Tell us about that. What brought you up there? Were you still married at that time?
Yeah. I went up there with Tommy Chase -- this guy around here named Chase. He's dead now. A piano player. He played piano and trumpet.
He took a band up there?
Phillips - 196

Yeah, he got... You know how in the summertime they want bands to come up on those jobs. You know what I mean. So he got some musicians together. He got me, he got Leo Williams, and he got another little young tenor player around here, he's dead now, named Sonny...
Leo Williams.
Leo Williams, yeah. He was a helluva tenor player.
Is that the guy who went into Eckstine's band?
No, no. That's Leo Parker.
But there was another Williams in Eckstine's band.
Another Williams?
I thought so.
No, Leo Williams was a helluva tenor player, but he laid around here. He played with Diz.
Who was the guy who got kind of sick after a while?
Oh, that's Leo Parker. He was a baritone player.
Well, don't get tied up with me.
